# The Consistency Hypothesis in Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#consistency-hypothesis)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v286/main/assets/xiao25a/xiao25a.pdf) · UAI 2025 publisher PDF, 16 pages including supplementary material; proceedings record identifies PMLR 286

**Reading coverage:** Sections 1-6, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-3, all supplementary text A.1-A.5/B and figure captions. Rendered Figures 10–12 inspected.

## Research question

Consistency-based confidence assumes that correct generations agree more than incorrect ones, but the assumption has several inequivalent meanings.

## Method

Defines Sim-Correct, Sim-Separate and label-free Sim-Any hypotheses using pairwise or aggregated similarities. Repeated random grouping and one-sided mean tests measure the fraction of groups supporting each hypothesis; geometric and harmonic aggregators provide confidence scores.

## Evaluation

Eight QA, summarization and SQL datasets. SQL experiments use Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD, with CodeLlama and fine-tuned DeepSeek, and label correctness by execution-result agreement. Confidence experiments report AUROC/AUARC using five random half-dataset evaluations.

## What the results support

Positive aggregate separation supports consistency as a useful ranking signal in the studied settings. Stronger label-aware statements are not directly usable at inference; practical Sim-Any support varies with model, metric, sampling and group size.

## Limits and qualifications

Dataset/group significance does not guarantee a correct individual answer. SQL labels inherit reference and single-database limitations; the learned-model comparison also changes model family and fine-tuning, limiting causal attribution to fine-tuning. Ranking metrics do not establish calibrated per-instance probabilities.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides diagnostic tests and simple confidence baselines for selective SQL generation, rather than a detector of missing information or user ambiguity.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
